subject: Action required: How to redirect inference traffic during multi-region cloud disruption
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@astrahealth.com>, ops@astra-corp.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Action required: How to redirect inference traffic during multi-region cloud disruption

Hi Tom / Astra ops team —

Thanks for your patience this morning. We observed a large cloud provider disruption affecting eu-west and several APAC zones starting ~08:15 UTC. Some customers (including Astra Health) may see elevated error rates or increased latency for requests routed to those zones.

Immediate ask: if you have any routing rules tied to region-specific endpoints (e.g., eu-west.*.redwoodapis.com or apac.*.redwoodapis.com), please follow the attached quick-checklist to temporarily route traffic to our global fallback endpoints to prevent timeouts. The checklist includes DNS TTL guidance and how to switch to the resilient endpoint we pushed at 08:40 UTC.

Summary of impact:
- eu-west: high error rate for new connections; partial backend saturation
- apac-southeast: intermittent 502s for long-running streams
- us-east: degraded latency for a small percentage of sessions (falling back handled automatically)

What we did:
- Enabled automatic fallback to global-render nodes for critical customers
- Reduced client-side keepalive thresholds to speed failover
- Published a resilient global endpoint: global.prod.redwoodapis.com (see checklist)

Next steps for you (short):
1) Point inference traffic at global.prod.redwoodapis.com (CNAME or direct host)
2) Decrease DNS TTL to 60s if you control DNS and plan to revert quickly
3) Disable region-specific sticky routing in your load balancer for 30m

We attached: reroute-checklist.pdf (quick commands), regional-traffic-map.png (visual), incident-timeline.csv (raw events).

If you want, we can schedule a 15-min call right now to walk through DNS and LB changes — Marissa can join to help coordinate.

Sorry again for the disruption; were treating this as high priority.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Reliability (Redwood Inference)
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom@astrahealth.com>, ops@astra-corp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action required: How to redirect inference traffic during multi-region cloud disruption

Tom / Astra ops —

Following up with the specific technical steps for the engineering team. This is what we've validated in staging and rolled out to affected customers: 

1) Fallback host (recommended): global.prod.redwoodapis.com:443
   - TLS certs already provisioned for customer hostnames via SNI; no changes required for host headers.
2) DNS CNAME approach: set your inference domain (e.g., api.astra-inference.com) -> CNAME -> global.prod.redwoodapis.com; set TTL to 60s.
3) Load balancer adjustments: remove region affinity for 30-45 minutes. If you run edge proxies, set health-check window to 10s for faster failover.
4) SDKs: our SDKs will honor explicit host override if you prefer (env REDWOOD_HOST=global.prod.redwoodapis.com).

Known caveat: streaming sessions in-flight may still experience truncation; recommend reconnects after switching. We increased token retry window on the server-side for customers that cannot reconnect quickly.

Attached checklist includes curl examples and an nginx config snippet. If your infra team wants, I can paste the exact nginx block in this thread.

— Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@astrahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, ops@astra-corp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action required: How to redirect inference traffic during multi-region cloud disruption

Hey team —

Thanks for the quick guidance. We're making the DNS switch now (TTL 60s). A couple quick questions: 
- Is there a recommended max QPS per connection to global.prod?
- Will logs show which requests were rerouted so we can reconcile with our tracing?

Also, we saw two production streams drop ~09:05 UTC; are those covered by the retry window you mentioned?

I'll update once the CNAME propagation finishes. Appreciate the help.

— Tom
Ops Lead, Astra Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@astrahealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action required: How to redirect inference traffic during multi-region cloud disruption

Tom —

Were tracking the two dropped streams and will share a reconciliation. For immediate reassurance: we enabled a temporal retry window and increased per-tenant connection quotas on the fallback nodes so you should not see throttling related to reroute. If you do, reply-all and well escalate to on-call infra.

Separately, as part of our incident policy, were offering affected customers a one-time service credit equivalent to two days of inference spend for visible outages linked to provider issues. Marissa will follow up with a short form to capture billing account and preferred credit handling.

— Aditya Rao
Head of Customer Success
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@astrahealth.com>, Nina Patel <nina@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final update and post-incident follow-up: routing restored, next steps

Hi Tom / Nina —

Final update from the Redwood side: the cloud provider cleared the issue in eu-west and APAC at ~03:20 UTC this morning and we verified normal request rates by 05:10 UTC. Our telemetry shows Astra Health cut over to the global endpoint at 09:12 UTC yesterday and error rates returned to baseline shortly after.

What were delivering to you:
- Incident timeline (attached incident-timeline.csv) with our event timestamps and the provider's notifications
- A short postmortem with root cause analysis and permanent mitigations (link sent privately to your security contact)
- The reroute checklist we asked you to follow — please keep it for runbook updates.

Action items for Astra:
- Confirm whether you would like us to maintain a CNAME-based failover pre-wired in your account (we can prepare an editable Cloud DNS template).
- Fill the billing credit form Marissa will send; we will apply the two-day credit to the account upon receipt.

If youd like a 30-minute debrief, we can schedule with infra and CS tomorrow. Thanks for working through this with us.

Regards,
— Soojin
Head of Customer Reliability
soojin_lee@redwood.com
